newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF mission to visit Kiev Sept 16 - IMF.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to visit Kiev Sept 16 - IMF.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission due to visit Kiev on September 16 will concentrate on Ukraine's request for an Extended Fund Facility (EFF) of between $2.5 and $3 billion, an IMF official said on Tuesday.
"The mission will focus on making progress on EFF negotiations," resident representative Alex Sundakov told Reuters.
Sundakov would not comment on Ukraine's request for $1.5 billion to back the permanent hryvnia currency, which is replacing the karbovanets.
The karbovanets is due to become obsolete on September 16.
Ukrainian officials have been confident about the approval of the currency stabilisation fund since the hryvnia was introduced on September 2.
Sundakov said the three-year EFF would, if granted, succeed Ukraine's $867-million stand-by programme, which is being disbursed in monthly tranches and set to extend into early 1997.
"It is a medium-term programme which concentrates more on economic growth," said Sundakov.
Ukraine has received about $2 billion in IMF credits since securing approval for its first market reform programme in 1994. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
